newsitem.title: PERU: Peru tops aim of 600,000 foreign tourists in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Peru tops aim of 600,000 foreign tourists in 1996.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Monday it had exceeded its goal of attracting 600,000 foreign tourists in 1996, up from 485,000 in 1995.
"We surpassed the target today and I believe that we will close the year with 650,000 or 660,000 tourists," said Industry and Tourism Minister Gustavo Caillaux.
He added that tourism revenues this year were expected to reach $900 million, up from $650 million last year.
Although traditionally popular for its archeological riches and dramatic Andean and jungle landscapes, Peru lost favor with foreign tourists following the outbreak of a violent guerrilla war in 1980.
However, the government's virtual defeat of leftist rebels since 1992, and the consequent reduction in violence, has given a boost to the tourist trade.
Caillaux said the government hoped to attract 750,000 foreign tourists in 1997.
